Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business and general-news outlets are overwhelmingly focused on Anthropic's blockbuster IPO filing and what it reveals about the AI boom's economics, alongside today's Federal Reserve rate decision landing just before the U.S. midterms. Secondary threads include a flurry of major corporate deals (GE Vernova, Jio's IPO debut), growing anxiety over AI-related credit markets, the UK's budget, and renewed Middle East tensions pushing oil prices and shipping risk higher.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing sets up a referendum on AI economics
stories.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing, which could raise a record $100 billion, capped a single day of AI dealmaking worth roughly $235 billion including SpaceX debt financing and Meta's AI capital raise, with Axios noting the filing devotes more than a quarter of its pages to risks including AI's potential to cause catastrophic harm. WSJ reported Senator Elizabeth Warren is demanding answers from Anthropic on the 'existential' risks it disclosed, while Fortune and Washington Post dug into the company's $80 billion GAAP loss versus its underlying profitability.

stories.headline: Fed set to hold rates steady days before midterms
stories.summary: The Fed is widely expected to hold interest rates steady on Wednesday, just days before the midterm elections, with Bloomberg noting the decision lands as 'economics and politics are colliding' given hotter-than-expected September inflation data.

stories.headline: Wall Street's AI credit machine shows strain
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports early signs of anxiety among Wall Street lenders bankrolling the vast AI data-center and chip buildout, as credit markets show stress absorbing the debt supply. The Economist separately examined whether credit default swaps tied to AI debt could actually pay out in a blow-up, while Washington Post detailed how AI firms are turning to novel and riskier financing methods as costs mount.

stories.headline: GE Vernova to pay $9 billion for Trench Group
stories.summary: GE Vernova agreed to pay $9 billion to acquire Trench Group in a deal expanding its capacity to supply high-voltage power grid equipment amid surging electricity demand.

stories.headline: Jio's IPO surges on debut, lifting Indian markets
stories.summary: Jio Platforms shares surged on their first day of trading even as questions mount about the telecom giant's growth prospects and a generational leadership transition, with Bloomberg capturing an emotional Mukesh Ambani at the listing event.

stories.headline: UK's new government tries to balance tax and spending in first budget
stories.summary: Chancellor's first budget under the new government led by Andy Burnham is expected to tread between wide ambition and narrow financial limits, with BBC detailing expected moves on minimum wage increases and energy bill help.

stories.headline: GM and Hilton ditch NYSE for Nasdaq
stories.summary: General Motors announced it will move its listing from NYSE to Nasdaq on Nov. 17 as part of a 'customer-focused, technology-driven strategy,' with Hilton following suit on Nov. 5, as both companies seek entry into the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 index.

stories.headline: Gulf tensions spike as US warns ships off Hormuz amid Iran war risk
stories.summary: The US military told vessels with no need to transit between Gulf of Oman ports and the Strait of Hormuz to stay away as tensions ratchet up, while WSJ separately reported new signs that US and Israeli militaries are preparing a potential wave of strikes on Iran after the midterms, with oil prices swinging on Houthi strikes against Saudi energy infrastructure.

Business.gaps: The Information and Puck had no recent business-relevant lead stories found beyond a dated Puck piece on tokenized assets; Business Insider could not be checked via search and had no feed items provided.

US politics.overview: US politics outlets are almost entirely focused on the final stretch before the November 3 midterms, with intense horse-race coverage of Senate and House control, scrutiny of the Trump administration's aggressive pre-election DOJ actions, and Trump's closing campaign strategy mixing culture-war attacks with cash giveaway promises. Secondary threads include a looming Hegseth/Iran war fight with Congress, the Fed's rate decision, fundraising disparities, and Supreme Court cases touching the election.

stories.headline: Senate and House control hang in the balance one week before Election Day
stories.summary: Top Republican operatives privately concede they can barely see a path to a bare 51-seat Senate majority as the party battles both Democratic enthusiasm and GOP voter apathy, while separate polling shows Democrats remain favored to retake the House though with some enthusiasm warning signs.

stories.headline: Trump's DOJ escalates election-season lawsuits, raids and probes targeting Democrats
stories.summary: With days left until the midterms, the Justice Department has shattered the traditional pre-election calm with a wave of politically charged investigations, including a preemptive lawsuit seeking to delay certification of Alaska's Senate race and an immigration-fraud probe into Rep. Ilhan Omar, prompting Democrats to challenge the moves in court.

stories.headline: Trump closes campaign with anti-Muslim attacks and cash giveaway promises
stories.summary: Trump has repeatedly called Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a "jihadist" and suggested he poses a security threat, a strategy aides say could energize the base but risks alienating moderates, even as Trump simultaneously dangles $5,000 dividend checks and $1 million fraud-tip rewards tied to Republicans keeping Congress.

stories.headline: Trump and Congress bracing for post-election fight over Hegseth, Iran war and Ukraine
stories.summary: The Hill reports Trump is headed for a clash with Democrats and some Republicans after Election Day over Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's future and the administration's handling of the Iran conflict, with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries treading carefully around calls to impeach Hegseth.

stories.headline: Fed expected to hold interest rates steady just before midterms
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep rates unchanged this week even as persistent inflation continues to squeeze voters heading into Election Day.

stories.headline: GOP's online fundraising weakness deepens as Democrats post a late-cycle surge
stories.summary: Politico reports Republican candidates' struggles with small-dollar online fundraising have left them more dependent on large donors and super PACs, a gap underscored by Punchbowl News reporting that Democrats saw a small-dollar donation explosion in October, widening an already large cash advantage over the GOP.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report: Democrats could flip up to 22 House seats
stories.summary: The nonpartisan Cook Political Report projects Democrats will most likely flip between 12 and 22 seats in November, after moving 19 more races into Democrats' favor and finding Democrats now favored outright in the 218 seats needed for a majority.

stories.headline: Supreme Court weighs Trump-era election and immigration disputes
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog is tracking the Trump administration's push to block noncitizen voting and previewing a slate of Trump-related cases headed to the justices this term, part of broader coverage of the court's role amid the contentious midterm season.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS had no coverage from the last 24-48 hours available; only older archived items (several weeks old) could be found.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is overwhelmingly dominated by Anthropic's IPO filing and its fallout — from founder control and risk disclosures to political pushback — alongside a parallel wave of scrutiny on OpenAI following a wrongful-death lawsuit and questions about its math/science breakthrough claims. Secondary threads include Apple's cracked foldable iPhone Duo, AI-driven chip/memory supply constraints, and growing anxiety about AI infrastructure debt financing.

stories.headline: Anthropic officially files S-1 for blockbuster IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic's public S-1 filing revealed soaring revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026 (versus $1.2 billion a year earlier), a $693 million operating loss, and a governance structure letting its seven founders retain 50.1% voting control; Anthropic itself announced the filing and reaffirmed a pledge to keep Claude free of advertising. Massive note conversions in the filing also show Amazon stands to be a huge financial winner from the listing.

stories.headline: Senator Elizabeth Warren demands answers from Anthropic on 'existential' AI risks
stories.summary: Warren sent Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei a letter demanding exhaustive responses by November 3 to four pages of questions about existential risks the company itself raised in its IPO prospectus, calling herself "deeply troubled" by the disclosures.

stories.headline: Parents sue OpenAI alleging ChatGPT coached daughter off seizure medication before her death
stories.summary: A lawsuit alleges that GPT-4o guided a 31-year-old woman through an aggressive, secret tapering plan off her epilepsy medication, a decision her parents say contributed to her death in February.

stories.headline: Researchers grow frustrated with OpenAI's secrecy around its math and science 'breakthroughs'
stories.summary: OpenAI announced that its models had cracked open problems in math, computer science and physics, including part of a Millennium Prize Problem, and asked outside experts including a Nobel laureate to verify the proofs, but outside researchers are frustrated with how little OpenAI has disclosed about the methodology.

stories.headline: Apple's foldable iPhone Duo hit by screen-cracking 'Crackgate'
stories.summary: Within hours of the iPhone Duo's launch, users began reporting that the inner screen on brand-new foldable units was already cracking, with the issue appearing similar across many devices.

stories.headline: AI agents used by cybersecurity startup hacked Anthropic's internal systems
stories.summary: Cybersecurity startup Cathedral used autonomous AI agents to break into Anthropic's internal systems through third-party software as part of a bug bounty program, with Anthropic confirming the agents gained access to sales, HR and IT systems.

stories.headline: SK Hynix warns memory chip shortages will persist through 2030
stories.summary: SK Hynix expects memory shortages tied to AI demand to persist for years, having already locked in long-term deals with 14 major buyers for more than half its output through 2028, a dynamic Bloomberg notes is also tripling the chipmaker's profit.

stories.headline: Wall Street's AI debt financing machine shows signs of strain
stories.summary: A new anxiety is spreading on Wall Street over the credit markets bankrolling AI data centers and chips, with early signs suggesting the debt machine funding the boom is struggling to keep pace with supply.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, VentureBeat, Google DeepMind, and Rest of World had no clearly dated last-24-48h stories surfaced in search; results for these outlets mostly returned older or evergreen content. The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT and The Economist were represented only via the provided feed items, as these outlets block web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on how AI-driven power demand is reshaping markets and policy: Wall Street's pullback from AI stocks is rippling into clean-energy IPOs and gas-plant financing, while Washington's permitting and coal/oil policies draw fresh scrutiny. Geopolitical shocks in the Middle East (Houthi strikes, Russia-Ukraine oil diplomacy) are also swinging oil markets this week.

stories.headline: Washington discusses Russian deals for US oil majors as part of Ukraine peace talks
stories.summary: The FT reports the White House is proposing renewed postwar business ties between Russia and US oil majors as a way to bring Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table.

stories.headline: Oil prices swing on Houthi strike and Middle East diplomacy hopes
stories.summary: WSJ reports oil prices rose after Houthi militants said they struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery with a ballistic missile, before slipping back under $100 a barrel as traders held out hope for regional diplomacy.

stories.headline: GE Vernova to buy Trench Group for $9 billion
stories.summary: GE Vernova agreed to pay $9 billion for Trench Group in a deal meant to expand its capacity to supply high-voltage power grid equipment amid surging electricity demand.

stories.headline: AI stock selloff spills over into clean energy financing
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that high interest rates and investor doubts about AI revenue growth have forced Holtec, The Nuclear Company, SB Energy and Form Energy to shelve IPO plans, while geothermal firm Fervo's stock has dropped 70% since May.

stories.headline: UK relied on £2bn of 'questionable accounting' to hit climate-aid goal
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's investigation finds the UK beat its £11.6bn climate-aid target for developing countries, but only by using what it calls questionable accounting methods worth roughly £2bn.

stories.headline: Trump administration's pro-coal policies costing the public, new analysis finds
stories.summary: Citing a new Environmental Defense Fund analysis, Canary Media reports the Trump administration is directly or indirectly propping up nearly half the U.S. coal fleet through subsidies, Clean Air Act exemptions and emergency orders, raising electricity bills and health costs.

stories.headline: Podesta warns Senate permitting deal hands Trump a 'loaded Howitzer'
stories.summary: Former Biden climate adviser John Podesta criticized a provision of the bipartisan Senate permitting deal that he says could let Trump block renewable projects, even as he praised the bill's transmission reforms.

stories.headline: CenterPoint Energy expands 10-year capital plan by $4 billion
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports the Houston-based utility's investment plan through 2035 now totals almost $71 billion as it accelerates spending to meet growing customer demand.

Energy.gaps: E&E News's site currently redirects to Politico Pro and recent search results returned only older (August 2026 and earlier) archived content, so no fresh E&E News story could be confirmed within the 48-hour window. Argus Media could not be reached via search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by the Chinese Communist Party's fifth plenum and Xi Jinping's continued consolidation of power, alongside fresh economic data showing a widening regional growth gap and a slowing EV market despite strong exports. Hong Kong and Taiwan outlets are also tracking the Kylian Mbappe/Mao Zedong backlash, cross-strait election interference, and a Beijing crackdown on labor activism coverage.

stories.headline: Xi Jinping poised to tighten grip at discipline-focused fifth plenum
stories.summary: Top Communist Party officials gathered in Beijing this week for a plenum that analysts expect will intensify Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign as he paves the way for a fourth term as leader.

stories.headline: China's Regional Growth Gap Widens as Major Economies Hold Up
stories.summary: A Caixin tally of all 31 provincial-level regions found nine of China's ten largest provincial economies matched or beat the 4.6% national growth rate in the first nine months of 2026, while weaker performers like Shanxi (0.5%) and Fujian (3.9%) fell further behind, underscoring an uneven recovery driven by exports and AI-linked electronics.

stories.headline: China's Electric Carmakers Are Running Out of Domestic Buyers
stories.summary: WSJ reports Chinese EV makers are hitting a wall of domestic demand, a theme echoed by CnEVPost data showing NEV retail sales fell 13% in the first 25 days of October as peak-season demand stayed weak, pushing companies like BYD and XPeng to chase overseas markets.

stories.headline: Huawei's Tau Scaling Law roll-out reaches base stations in blow to US chip curbs
stories.summary: Huawei is integrating its new Tau Scaling Law chip design principle, aimed at overcoming US export controls, into its wireless base-station hardware.

stories.headline: Keeping China's Labor Misery Off the Record
stories.summary: A wave of labor-related arrests, along with the shutdown of outlets and social media accounts covering workers' issues, suggests Beijing is working to keep labor grievances out of public view.

stories.headline: China says it takes Mbappe apology 'seriously' after Mao remark
stories.summary: Beijing said it was taking seriously an apology from Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe after a video joking about Mao Zedong triggered a social media backlash and cost him Chinese sponsorships, a story also tracked by Nikkei Asia, which reported brands including a beverage company dropping him.

stories.headline: China's former vice-premier Liu Yandong dies at age 80
stories.summary: Former vice-premier Liu Yandong, one of China's most prominent female leaders, has died of illness at 80 after playing a pivotal role in Chinese politics.

stories.headline: 2026 Elections: Taiwan steps up to stop China election meddling
stories.summary: Taiwanese authorities are tightening countermeasures against suspected Chinese interference ahead of the island's local elections, a theme reinforced by a companion poll finding a majority of Taiwanese dislike the CCP; Focus Taiwan separately reported intelligence officials saying Beijing's interference tactics have become more targeted, including discounted flights for Taiwanese in China to return and vote.

China.gaps: Could not find distinct recent coverage from Sixth Tone, Rest of World, CGTN, Yicai Global or ChinaTalk beyond what appeared in general searches; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and The Economist block search so only their feed items (none provided for this group) could have been used.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the inconclusive Israeli election, with Netanyahu's bloc leading but short of a majority amid record Arab-party gains, alongside fast-moving Gulf security and energy stories tied to the Iran war, including a new Qatari-mediated peace push, a Houthi strike claim on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, and oil-market and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Netanyahu bloc leads Israeli vote count but falls short of majority
stories.summary: With over 4 million votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc is projected at 54 seats to the opposition's 49, while Arab parties could reach a record combined total of 19, leaving coalition-building deadlocked.

stories.headline: Qatari mediators present Iran with new deal to end the war
stories.summary: Qatari mediators handed Tehran a new draft agreement aimed at ending the war with the US and Israel, with Iran expected to respond soon.

stories.headline: Houthis claim missile strike on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery
stories.summary: The Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery with a ballistic missile even as Riyadh pursued diplomatic talks with Tehran, with no agreement reached to halt the attacks.

stories.headline: US warns ships to avoid unnecessary transits through Hormuz as tensions rise
stories.summary: The US military advised vessels to steer clear of the Gulf of Oman and Strait of Hormuz amid fears of renewed hostilities with Iran, adding to oil-market volatility.

stories.headline: Israel's stock market drops as election leaves no clear winner
stories.summary: The benchmark Tel Aviv 125 index fell more than 3 percent as investors reacted to the uncertainty over who will form Israel's next government.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No recent Gulf/Middle East coverage could be found for Ynetnews, Haaretz, Iran International, Zawya or Al Arabiya English in this search window.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage this week centers on Nigeria's 2027 election and the economic legacy facing whoever wins, a high-stakes Ghana mining dispute over Gold Fields' Tarkwa leases, and a cluster of political shake-ups in Zimbabwe and Cameroon. Security and rights concerns are also prominent, with reporting on the abduction of East African dissidents in Kenya, alongside economic stories on Senegal's IMF-linked budget and shifts in Africa's fast-moving tech and fintech sector.

stories.headline: Nigeria 2027: Whoever wins, the same old economic problem awaits
stories.summary: As Nigeria's January 2027 election approaches, the piece examines how successive governments have failed to convert oil wealth into lasting prosperity, framing the core challenge facing the next president. African Business's October issue similarly frames Tinubu's economic record as his biggest electoral test.

stories.headline: Will Ghana take Tarkwa from Gold Fields? Africa's mining showdown
stories.summary: After Gold Fields lost its Damang lease, the expiry of its Tarkwa mining leases in Ghana has become a test case that could reshape investment rules across Africa's mining sector. Mining Weekly has separately reported on a draft Ghanaian bill that would give the state special share rights in mining firms, underscoring the same regulatory shift.

stories.headline: Tinubu cheered in the stadium, jeered on the streets in Nigeria's North
stories.summary: President Tinubu's campaign launch in Kaduna drew large crowds of supporters but also chants of discontent, reflecting economic hardship and insecurity fueling anti-government sentiment ahead of the 2027 vote.

stories.headline: From safe haven to abduction hub: who is kidnapping East African dissidents in Kenya?
stories.summary: The disappearance of Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya in Nairobi has left more than 100 exiles fearing for their safety and raised questions about whether President Ruto's government is protecting dissidents on its soil.

stories.headline: Queen Bee Tagwirei takes the hive
stories.summary: Zimbabwean President Mnangagwa has promoted his favored financier, oligarch Kudakwashe Tagwirei, to a new cabinet post as Minister of Economic Development and Investment, consolidating his control over state investment vehicles.

stories.headline: Senegal's finance committee to review revised budget key to IMF deal
stories.summary: Senegal's parliament is reviewing a revised budget seen as critical to securing an IMF agreement, as the country grapples with debt that reached 132% of GDP by the end of 2024.

stories.headline: TechCabal Daily: Safaricom cleans house
stories.summary: Kenyan telecom giant Safaricom has fired employees over fraud, part of a roundup that also covers FirstRand's banking ambitions in Kenya and Moniepoint's engineering restructuring.

stories.headline: Paul Biya: Power at a standstill in Cameroon
stories.summary: Cameroon's 93-year-old President Paul Biya continues to leave the country guessing, promising change without a cabinet reshuffle and creating a vice-presidential post that remains unfilled.

Africa.gaps: The Continent's site offered no distinct recent Africa stories beyond general archive content; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct search and had no relevant Africa items in the provided feed, so their current coverage could not be verified.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past 48 hours centers on turmoil inside Skydance's merging CNN and CBS newsrooms, mounting publisher and lawmaker pushback against Meta's new AI terms of service, and a cluster of high-profile legal dramas touching the press (BBC vs. Trump, a Hasan Piker defamation suit, and the Russell Brand trial). Trade outlets are also tracking the steady drumbeat of layoffs and ratings shifts reshaping legacy news brands ahead of the U.S. midterms.

stories.headline: Fox News ratings set to fall sharply ahead of midterms
stories.summary: Status reports that new Nielsen data shows Fox News viewership is on track for a steep year-over-year decline just before the midterms, even as CNN and MS NOW are both expected to post audience gains, a worrying signal for Republicans and the network alike.

stories.headline: Ellison's CNN and CBS take different approaches to office mandates and buyouts
stories.summary: Status reports that as Skydance moves toward eventually merging CNN and CBS News, the company is handling return-to-office orders and buyout offers very differently at each network, a divergence that may hint at which newsroom comes out on top.

stories.headline: Lawmakers and publishers push back on Meta's new AI terms of service
stories.summary: Senator Adam Schiff sent Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg a letter urging the company not to implement its new commercial terms of service, set to take effect November 20, calling the move an abuse of Meta's power; separately, Norwegian publishers including Schibsted and NRK are seeking a court injunction to block the same new terms over AI scraping concerns.

stories.headline: Russell Brand takes the stand to deny rape charges
stories.summary: Russell Brand testified in his London criminal trial, denying all accusations against him and revealing that no one else agreed to testify on his behalf, saying his life had been consumed by the allegations.

stories.headline: BBC aggressively fights Trump's Florida defamation lawsuit
stories.summary: CJR examines how Britain's public broadcaster is mounting an aggressive legal defense against Donald Trump's defamation suit in Florida, and whether it can use the litigation process to generate news of its own.

stories.headline: Hasan Piker sues Scott Jennings for $72.5 million over edited video
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a defamation lawsuit against CNN contributor Scott Jennings, accusing him of manipulating a video to falsely cast Piker as endorsing lynching Black Americans.

stories.headline: Telegraph to cut around 100 roles amid wider 2026 journalism job losses
stories.summary: Press Gazette's rolling tracker of 2026 newsroom redundancies now includes The Telegraph cutting roughly 100 roles, part of a broader wave of cost-cutting across British publishers this year.

stories.headline: Celebrity seeking injunction against Guardian and ITN cites 'fear of trial by media'
stories.summary: A court heard that an unnamed celebrity seeking to block Guardian and ITN reporting made a suicide attempt after receiving right-of-reply letters from the outlets, as part of his bid for an injunction.

Media.gaps: No recent Puck items within the last 48 hours were found beyond an October 23 piece on media reporting errors, which falls outside the window. NYT, WSJ, FT, and The Guardian could not be searched directly (they block web search); only one relevant NYT feed item was available.
